rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant stepped bar across all four views, so it clears the multi-view coherence gate. The parcel is contained and the mass aligns reasonably with the oblique footprint, but the gesture is still mostly a generic stepped extrusion. The main weakness is programmatic: the blue access edge is not answered by a convincing public void, court, undercut, or entry seam; the ground condition stays sealed and the open-space figure is very limited. Still, the silhouette and hierarchy are legible, the stepping is continuous rather than fragmentary, and the mass could plausibly support compact neighborhood living/commercial use. It is not a gymnasium or other long-span hall typology, so no missing_program_section failure applies. The references support courtyard-active commercial/neighborhood edges more than tower-like stacking; the bridge reference is only useful as a counterfactual to motivate a clearer seam or notch at the access side.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact massing with a readable public edge and a courtyard-like outdoor room; good precedent for neighborhood-active ground logic.
Low, courtyard-oriented street building with interior/exterior spillover and a legible enclosure sequence.
